provenance.what: Rows of the node-graph opening-camera law: graph bounds + viewport + stored camera -> the camera a surface opens on.
provenance.law: A stored camera is adopted only when it already shows at least `minCoverage` of the graph's own area; otherwise the graph is fitted with `paddingPx` of screen margin per side and the zoom clamped to the canvas camera range. `refits` is the separate, far stricter gate an ALREADY LIVE camera passes when the graph changed under it (an example switch).
provenance.calibration: `minCoverage` 0.85 is the one judgement call here. The live generation3d boot camera (x=94.75 y=-97.5 zoom=1.78 in a 483x814 pane) covers 0.570 of its own graph and shows one node of seven, so 0.6 would have decided it by 0.03; 0.85 decides it by 0.28 and still adopts a camera with a sliver of the graph off the edge.
provenance.publication: A surface that FITS must publish the camera it computed. A flow surface carries two camera copies — the FlowHost fixture camera (the authority: what screen-to-world projects with, what every dag rebuild re-seeds the dag copy from, and what the renderer publishes as nodeGraphViewport) and the DagHost fixture camera (the derived copy the paint reads). `surfaceRows` pins that a fit lands on BOTH, so a Fit graph can never publish the pre-fit camera while painting the fitted one.

rows.name: a-surface-with-no-stored-camera-fits-its-whole-graph
rows.why: The first attach of a graph nobody has framed yet must show all of it, not the world origin.

rows.name: a-stored-camera-that-already-frames-the-graph-is-adopted
rows.why: A camera the viewer set and that still shows the graph is never overridden.

rows.name: a-stored-camera-with-a-small-overhang-is-still-adopted
rows.why: The framing test is a coverage threshold, not exact containment; a sliver off the edge is tolerated.

rows.name: a-stored-camera-that-only-shows-three-quarters-is-replaced-by-the-fit
rows.why: Three quarters is not 'framed'. The live generation3d boot camera measures 0.570 of its graph.

rows.name: a-stored-camera-showing-half-the-graph-is-replaced-by-the-fit
rows.why: The boot defect this law closes: the stored camera shows one node of seven and still wins.

rows.name: a-stored-camera-that-left-the-graph-entirely-is-replaced-and-would-refit
rows.why: An example switch can move the whole graph out of view; zero coverage refits even a live camera.

rows.name: a-graph-larger-than-the-zoom-floor-is-centred-not-over-zoomed
rows.why: fit_camera clamps to the canvas camera range instead of returning an unusable zoom.

rows.name: a-single-node-graph-fits-to-its-own-box
rows.why: One node is still content; the fit frames it rather than falling back to zoom 1.

rows.name: a-zero-height-graph-is-measured-on-the-axis-it-has
rows.why: A row of nodes at one y must not read as zero coverage and refit forever.

rows.name: an-empty-graph-leaves-the-stored-camera-alone
rows.why: Nothing to frame is not a reason to move the viewer's camera.

surfaceRows.name: fit-after-the-boot-camera-publishes-the-camera-it-computed
surfaceRows.why: The wgpu Fit graph control published the scene's own boot camera (x=94.75 y=-97.5 zoom=1.78) while the fit it had just computed stayed on the derived paint copy.

surfaceRows.name: fit-after-a-zoom-out-publishes-the-camera-it-computed
surfaceRows.why: A viewer who zoomed far out must get the whole graph back, not the camera the document shipped with.

surfaceRows.name: fit-after-a-pan-off-the-graph-publishes-the-camera-it-computed
surfaceRows.why: The pan that makes the defect visible: every node is off screen, so the published camera and the painted camera must both be the fit.

surfaceRows.name: a-second-fit-changes-nothing
surfaceRows.why: A fit is idempotent: pressing Fit graph twice must not drift the camera, which it would if the two copies disagreed.

fitAction.what: The framework `fitGraph` action: ONE declared action every node-graph window kind offers (palette, window toolbar, the F chord), executed by both renderers through the same camera law as `rows`, and persisted like a wheel zoom through `nodeGraphViewport`.
fitAction.law: Unlike the opening camera, an explicit fit ignores the stored camera: it always installs fit_camera(content, viewport, paddingPx); an empty graph has nothing to frame and changes nothing.
implementations: .🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END/node-graph-fit-oracle.py — the independent Python oracle that recomputes every fitRows expectation

fitRows.name: two-nodes-fill-a-narrow-pane-by-width
fitRows.why: The wider axis decides the zoom and the centre is the middle of the union of both node boxes.

fitRows.name: a-single-node-is-centred-and-enlarged
fitRows.why: One node has extent on both axes; the tighter one decides.

fitRows.name: a-row-of-zero-height-nodes-is-framed-by-width-alone
fitRows.why: Degenerate content (no vertical extent) must not read as an infinite zoom.

fitRows.name: a-single-point-falls-back-to-unit-zoom
fitRows.why: No extent on either axis has no scale to frame: zoom 1, centred on the point.

fitRows.name: a-graph-past-the-zoom-out-floor-is-centred-not-over-zoomed
fitRows.why: The fit is clamped to the canvas camera range.

fitRows.name: a-tiny-graph-is-capped-at-the-zoom-in-ceiling
fitRows.why: The fit is clamped to the canvas camera range.

fitRows.name: a-pane-smaller-than-its-padding-still-answers-a-camera
fitRows.why: Usable pane size is floored at one pixel per axis, so a collapsed window never divides by zero.

fitRows.name: an-explicit-fit-ignores-a-stored-camera-that-already-frames-the-graph
fitRows.why: The opening-camera law adopts this stored camera; the Fit control must not.

fitRows.name: an-empty-graph-has-nothing-to-frame
fitRows.why: No nodes, no camera change, nothing to persist.
